stages.ix_title: Choose the r-control sentence that matches the picture
stages.choice_rule: Four unique sentences and one answer_index. Words come from the roots list, allowed_extra_words, or the NAME token. Each sentence has one whole r-control word spelled ar, er, ir, or, and ur. Media is a single lemma that appears in the correct sentence only, and that sentence is true of a plain picture of the lemma. Stems are tap cues of at most ten words and do not describe the picture. Vary the answer_index. Some tier 3 stems may use <NAME> with swap slot NAME. Set explain_key to ar_word, er_word, ir_word, or_word, or ur_word to match the correct word. No IPA, no isolated sounds, and no audio files.

roots: Use exactly four different sentences, and make exactly one of them name the picture lemma.
Every sentence must use the roots word list or allowed_extra_words and stay under sixty characters.
Put one whole r-control word in every sentence, spelled ar, er, ir, or, and ur. Never use IPA or an isolated sound.
Tier 1 wrong sentences name something very different. Tier 2 wrong sentences keep the frame and change the r-control word. Tier 3 wrong sentences are near misses such as car, card, and cart.
The correct sentence must be true of a plain picture of the lemma. Do not add details the picture may not show.
Do not describe the picture in the stem. The picture is only a media lemma. Do not invent audio files.
Keep the kid world to school, home, food, pets, play, family, and weather. No brands and no real personal names.

tier_rules.1: Short stems of three to five words and short sentences. The other three sentences name very different things, so the picture match is easy to see.
tier_rules.2: Stems of about six words. Sentences share a frame, and distractors swap in another r-control word, including two-syllable words such as teacher, sister, and morning. Only one sentence names the picture.
tier_rules.3: Stems of seven to ten words. Distractors are near-miss r-control spellings in the same frame, such as car, card, cart, and jar, or bird and girl. Exactly one sentence names the picture lemma.

ar_word.en: Read the whole ar word. The right sentence names the picture, not a look-alike word.

er_word.en: Read the whole er word. The right sentence names the picture, not a different er word.

or_word.en: Read the whole or word, as in horse or corn. The right sentence names the picture.
